items.title: Union Minister Piyush Goyal Holds Trade and Investment Talks in the Netherlands
items.summary: The visit featured engagements with stakeholders in the maritime and logistics sector in Rotterdam, interaction with the Indian community in Amsterdam, and media engagement. As part of his programme in Rotterdam, Shri Piyush Goyal undertook a tour of the Port of Rotterdam, accompanied by its Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Boudewijn Siemons.

facts.text: The visit highlighted the strategic importance of Rotterdam, Europe's largest port, as a gateway for Indian goods to the European market and a key hub for international trade and global supply chains.
The Minister's visit to the Port of Rotterdam underscored the Netherlands' strategic importance as a gateway to Europe, particularly in the context of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement.

With the Agreement expected to create significant new opportunities for Indian exporters, the Netherlands' world-class ports, logistics infrastructure and connectivity with European markets can play an important role in facilitating increased trade flows and strengthening India-Europe supply chains.
The Minister also attended an Indian community interaction hosted by the Embassy of India over high tea at the Waldorf Astoria Amsterdam, with approximately 70 participants.

Mr. Vyacheslav Volodin, Chairman of the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation. During the meeting, Indian and Russian Parliamentary Delegations underscored the need for strengthening cooperation at global fora and collective efforts to combat terrorism.

facts.text: Extending a warm welcome to Mr. Volodin and his Delegation on behalf of the Parliament of India and 1.4 billion Indians, Shri Birla highlighted the special and time-tested friendship between India and Russia, rooted in mutual trust, respect and shared aspirations.
During the meeting, Shri Birla also highlighted opportunities for further strengthening bilateral cooperation in nuclear energy, industry and other sectors.
Alongside high-level plenary sessions, parallel meetings and bilateral exchanges, the conference would also feature a cultural programme.
The conference will conclude on 27 October, 2026.
